thousand numeral

also a thousand, two thousand, thousands, three thousand, a thousand people, a mile (a thousand paces), ten thousand, a hundred thousand, 2,000, 10,000, 100,000

classical

Traupman 253

mīlle

adjective, indeclinable, declension

a thousand

A thousand agrees like any number: mīlle hominēs, a thousand people. From two thousand on, the plural mīlia is a noun and takes the genitive (see below). mīlle with a genitive is the rarer use.

Other words

  • mīlia, mīlium n. pl. + gen. — thousands: two thousand, three thousand

    noun, third declension, plural (dat. and abl. mīlibus), with the genitive · classical · Plin. Ep. 3.1.4: mīlia passuum tria

    duo mīlia hominum, two thousand people; tria mīlia passuum, three miles (three thousand paces).

Examples

  • duo mīlia

    two thousandTraupman 253

  • Mīlle annōs, tata? Quam multōs! — Multōs vērō, immō plūrimōs.

    A thousand years, Dad? So many! — Many indeed; very many.composed

  • ambulat mīlia passuum tria

    he walks three milesPlin. Ep. 3.1.4

  • nam dē mīlle fabae modiīs cum surripis ūnum, damnum est, nōn facinus, mihi pactō lēnius istō

    for when you steal one peck from a thousand pecks of beans, it is a loss, not a crime, to me, by that milder reckoningHor. Ep. 1.16.55–56

  • ac prīmō placidum aequor mīlle nāvium rēmīs strepere

    and at first the calm sea roared with the oars of a thousand shipsTac. Ann. 2.23

  • decem mīlia

    ten thousandTraupman 253

  • centum mīlia

    a hundred thousandTraupman 253

See also million, six hundred, one of.
